edges.description: Zoonotically acquired B. abortus crosses a mucosal or cutaneous barrier and is taken up by phagocytes.
Intracellular persistence triggers a systemic inflammatory response.
Because the replicative niche is inside host phagocytes, it excludes poorly cell-penetrant agents and restricts effective therapy to intracellularly active drugs.
Persistent reticuloendothelial colonization produces the relapsing febrile illness that names the human disease.
The sustained systemic inflammatory response to persistent colonization produces the constitutional fatigue of acute B. abortus brucellosis.
Systemic infection produces the joint pain reported in PCR-confirmed B. abortus cases; the intervening synovial events are not resolved by any source cited here.
The relapsing febrile response is accompanied by the profuse sweating characteristic of the acute illness.
